name: Transactional test

subjectOf.text: Defined geographic borders for securities transactions, the overarching assumption behind Morrison, are an unstable basis for limiting the extraterritorial reach of either private litigation or government regulation.
subjectOf.abstract: Defined geographic borders for securities transactions—the overarching assumption behind the Morrison decision—are an unstable basis for limiting the extraterritorial reach of both private litigation and government regulation.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Richard W. Painter, Forum Competition and Choice of Law Competition in Securities Law after Morrison v. National Austral (2012). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2029983
scope_conditions: securities transactions whose location is contestable
applies to both private suits and regulatory enforcement

subjectOf.text: Geographic tests create the risk of a no man's land transaction: defendants may persuade the courts of every jurisdiction that the transaction took place outside their borders, leaving the transaction governed by no law and with no available forum.
subjectOf.abstract: Alternatively, defendants might successfully persuade courts in all jurisdictions that a transaction took place outside their borders or for some other reason outside their jurisdictions. Such a "no man's land" transaction would be governed by no law and there would be no forum.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Richard W. Painter, Forum Competition and Choice of Law Competition in Securities Law after Morrison v. National Austral (2012). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2029983
scope_conditions: transactions whose geographic location is ambiguous
courts in all candidate jurisdictions apply geographic tests

subjectOf.text: Morrison's transactional test could prove relatively short lived because it is rooted in geography while an increasing number of securities transactions defy geographical boundaries.
subjectOf.abstract: The transactional test in Morrison could be relatively short lived because it is rooted in geography and an increasing num- ber of securities transactions defy geographical boundaries.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Richard W. Painter, Forum Competition and Choice of Law Competition in Securities Law after Morrison v. National Austral (2012). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2029983
scope_conditions: transactions off organized exchanges and on exchanges that cross borders

subjectOf.text: The Second Circuit's Absolute Activist test, locating a transaction where title transfers or irrevocable liability is incurred, is easy to manipulate: parties can arrange for irrevocable liability to arise outside the United States, for example by conditioning liability on approval by an agent located abroad.
subjectOf.abstract: this test is easy to ma- nipulate by agreeing that one or both parties will take steps to create irrevocable liability outside the United States, for exam- ple, by making liability on the transaction contingent upon ap- proval of the transaction by an agent located outside the United States.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Richard W. Painter, Forum Competition and Choice of Law Competition in Securities Law after Morrison v. National Austral (2012). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2029983
scope_conditions: private securities transactions off organized exchanges

subjectOf.text: Choice of law should replace the geographically based transactional test in those circumstances where geography is ambiguous.
subjectOf.abstract: In sum, choice of law should replace the geographically- based transactional test in those circumstances where geogra- phy is ambiguous.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Richard W. Painter, Forum Competition and Choice of Law Competition in Securities Law after Morrison v. National Austral (2012). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2029983
scope_conditions: limited to transactions whose geographic location is ambiguous
